title: Smooth scheme morphisms induce formally smooth stalk maps
statement: Let $e:U\to X$ be a smooth morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] with smoothness as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], let $u\in U$, and put $x=e(u)$, $A=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and $B=\mathcal O_{U,u}$. The actual stalk homomorphism $e_u^\sharp:A\to B$ is formally smooth: for every commutative $A$-algebra $D$, every ideal $J\subset D$ with $J^2=0$, and every $A$-algebra homomorphism $B\to D/J$, there exists an $A$-algebra homomorphism $B\to D$ lifting it. No Noetherian, quasi-compactness, separation, or surjectivity hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 01V6 (lemma-smooth-characterize), affine smooth charts; more-morphisms.tex Tag 02H6 (lemma-smooth-formally-smooth); algebra.tex Tag 04EG (lemma-localization-formally-etale) and Tag 031H (lemma-compose-formally-smooth), applied to the localizations defining the stalks.
